chunks: From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The one granted time (mu'allah) is suspended after four months; if he wishes, he retains her with kindness, or releases her with grace. If he decides on divorce, it is a single revocable divorce, and he has the right to take her back.

key_terms.أَمْسَكَ بِمَعْرُوفٍ: Retains her in a good/fair manner
key_terms.أَمْلَكُ بِرَجْعَتِهَا: Has the right to take her back (revocable)
key_terms.الْمُؤَلَّى: A wife granted a specific period of time by her husband

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of divorce after the mu'allah period expires in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying that a husband forced to divorce his 'mu'allah' (wife granted a waiting period) after four months effects a single revocable divorce. This ruling emphasizes the husband's continued right of return (ruju') without requiring a new marriage contract, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the finality of the divorce count in this specific scenario. It highlights the balance between the husband's obligation to decide and the wife's protected status during the interim period.
